name: EUV lithography
thesis: Every sub-7nm logic chip and advanced DRAM is patterned on an EUV scanner, and ASML is the only company on earth that builds them — a textbook monopoly whose finite output rate is the hard ceiling on leading-edge capacity worldwide.

gauge.rationale: Sole-supplier concentration (Canon and Nikon exited EUV), >12-month lead times, and a record backlog that exceeds a full year of sales. Orders are surging and memory demand has now reached the lithography layer; the only relief is ASML's own production ramp.

metric.unit: Canon + Nikon hold <6% of litho and no EUV

why_it_gates: No EUV, no leading-edge logic and no advanced DRAM — the technology is the only way to pattern the smallest features at volume. Because ASML is the single global source and each scanner takes over a year to deliver, ASML's annual build rate physically caps how fast any foundry or memory maker, anywhere, can add cutting-edge capacity. The choke now extends into memory as HBM/DRAM demand reaches the lithography layer.

watchlist.name: Carl Zeiss SMT
watchlist.role: Sole EUV optics supplier to ASML

watchlist.name: SK Hynix
watchlist.role: Advanced-DRAM EUV demand now pulling tools

catalysts.text: ASML bookings and EUV mix signal how fast the order book is converting to revenue.
High-NA EUV high-volume ramp at $380M+/tool for sub-2nm nodes.
Export-control shifts on China continue to reshape ASML's demand mix.

what_loosens_it: ASML scaling its own output and High-NA productivity gains (fewer exposure passes per layer), or any moderation in AI capex that thins the order book.

developments.text: ASML reports record €38.8B year-end backlog (EUV 65%) and Q4 net bookings of €13.2B, including €7.4B of EUV — a ~250% order jump.
ASML raises 2026 outlook; analysts note customers are buying scarce 'machine time' and HBM/DRAM demand has reached the lithography layer.
